WRT 501: Ethical Foundations of UX explores the ethical considerations and responsibilities involved in designing digital experiences for users.
Through a combination of theoretical concepts, case studies, and practical exercises, students will gain an understanding of the ethical challenges faced by user experience designers and develop strategies to create user-centered and ethically sound designs.
Students will explore UX as a research and development method, especially as it relates to inclusive design and design justice.
Students will learn about foundational concepts in UX design, including terminology, history, and evolution of the field.
Using a critical lens, students will investigate issues of social justice, equity, sustainability, accessibility, and inclusion.
WRT 502: UX Research and Methods is an introduction to methods, research design, and data analysis in user experience projects, and aims to prepare professionals for designing, conducting, analyzing, and reporting their own user research studies.
This course will train students in how to determine the best methods and metrics for their projects, as well as design studies for effective data collection.

This course will also teach students how to communicate research results for decision-making purposes to a variety of stakeholders.
Students in this course will gain hands-on practice at every phase of the user research process, from identifying design problems or questions to developing their own test protocols, recruiting users, conducting user tests, and analyzing their results.
WRT 503: UX and Microcopy Writing is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the role and impact of effective writing in user-centered design.
Through a combination of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students will develop the skills necessary to create clear, concise, and engaging microcopy for digital interfaces and interactions.
WRT 504: Interaction Design focuses on the process of rapid, iterative design that keeps real people at the heart of creating content—a philosophy and design approach known as human-centered design.
Students in this course will learn agile design workflows, conduct rapid prototyping and wireframing, and share reflections on the process and results of user research meaningfully for public and industry audiences.

Students will gain hands-on, applied knowledge of the human-centered design process by creating their own design and refining it based on user feedback.

The science of pharmaceutical development is essential to the process of bringing a therapeutic entity from compound discovery to treatment in humans.
Most importantly, it seeks to create dosage forms for the compound that are safely consumed by humans (and animals), are stable until ingested, release the active drug product efficiently, avoid detrimental biologic interactions, have a consistent response, and have a known and controllable safety profile.
Advances in the knowledge and uses of injectable, biotech products have added a significant complexity to the drug development process.
In comparison to small molecule drug products, biological molecules have four levels of structure considerations making the development process much more complex and challenging.
